findings.evidence: The roadmap pins an integral lattice as a finite free `ℤ`-module (README lines 86–90, 144–147), but lines 55–57 require only additive groups; lines 73 and 177 add freeness/finiteness later, so `IsIntegralLattice` itself does not imply the promised API.
findings.fix: Define the predicate under `[Module.Free ℤ N] [Module.Finite ℤ N]` (with finite-dimensionality of `V` derived from the equivalence), then remove the repeated stronger-section assumptions from its consequences.
findings.issue: `IsIntegralLattice` omits the required finite-free hypothesis on `N`, so torsion or infinitely generated groups can satisfy the public predicate even though injectivity and discreteness are advertised as lattice consequences.

findings.evidence: Lines 37–39 force `N` and `V` into `Type u`, line 46 repeats this for `E`, and line 194 forces both target carriers into the same `u`; none of the tensor-product or map statements requires these equalities.
findings.fix: Give the carrier types independent universes, e.g. `N : Type u`, `V : Type v`, and separate universes for `N'` and `V'`; likewise generalize the private normed-space instance.
findings.issue: Using one universe `u` for `N`, `V`, `N'`, and `V'` needlessly prevents lattice maps and naturality across independently sized types.

summary: The predicate is broader than the roadmap’s integral-lattice object, while the entire API is unnecessarily restricted to types in one universe.
